claim: Standard LIMDU runs 6 months per 8105, plus a 2-month medical extension per 8111, for 8 months maximum without DES referral
quote: usually up to a cumulative total of 12 months, a MEB will be completed and forwarded to the PEB
fix: Say a Marine unlikely to return to full duty goes by MEB to the PEB, usually within a cumulative 12 months of light and limited duty (8102). A voluntary medical extension of a contract covers the TLD period up to 6 months. A DES referral or PEB wait up to 12 months, and short-term assessment or treatment up to 2 months (8111.1.a.3). Remove the 6 plus 2 equals 8 month rule.

claim: LIMDU does not normally exceed 8 months total without DES referral (6 month standard plus 2 month extension)
quote: usually up to a cumulative total of 12 months, a MEB will be completed and forwarded to the PEB
fix: Say a Marine unlikely to return to full duty goes by MEB to the PEB, usually within a cumulative 12 months of light and limited duty (8102). A voluntary medical extension of a contract covers the TLD period up to 6 months. A DES referral or PEB wait up to 12 months, and short-term assessment or treatment up to 2 months (8111.1.a.3). Remove the 6 plus 2 equals 8 month rule.

claim: Medical extension covers a 2-month period beyond standard LIMDU, and continued LIMDU beyond 8 months routes to DES
quote: For Marines in a TLD status, the length of the extension should cover the TLD period not to exceed 6 months.
fix: Say a Marine unlikely to return to full duty goes by MEB to the PEB, usually within a cumulative 12 months of light and limited duty (8102). A voluntary medical extension of a contract covers the TLD period up to 6 months. A DES referral or PEB wait up to 12 months, and short-term assessment or treatment up to 2 months (8111.1.a.3). Remove the 6 plus 2 equals 8 month rule.

claim: Extension exceeds 2 months means DES referral applies
quote: the length of the extension should cover the TLD period not to exceed 6 months
fix: The 2 month cap applies only to short-term health assessment or treatment. TLD extensions run to 6 months.

claim: MTF commander signs the LIMDU and medical extension determinations per 8110
quote: Commanding officers of Regular component Marines ... are authorized to approve the first extension on current contract
fix: The MTF recommends TLD (8110.2.a). The commanding officer approves the first extension. CMC (MMSR-4) approves second and later extensions. Use NAVMC 321M.

claim: MTF commander signs the LIMDU determination per 8110 (and 8104)
quote: MTF commanders ... are responsible for the following ... a. Recommends assignment to a period of TLD.
fix: MTF recommends, the MEB report (NAVMED 6100/5) directs TLD, and CMC (MMSR-4) reviews enlisted TLD beyond 12 months and officer TLD.

claim: MTF commander signs the medical extension determination; unit commander approves within policy bounds
quote: a medical extension NAVMC 321M form is required. The medical extension must be submitted to: (1) the commanding officer for first extensions
fix: Route NAVMC 321M to the commanding officer for the first extension and to CMC (MMSR-4) for the second and later. Reserve cases go to WWR RMED.

claim: PEB recommends PLD and EPLD; SECNAV and HQMC M&RA exercise retention authority; Monitor coordinates PCS per 8107
quote: The CMC (MMSR-4) may retain Marines found unfit for continued naval service by the PEB on active duty in a PLD status
fix: CMC (MMSR-4) approves PLD. CMC approves EPLD case by case. 8107 does not name the Monitor. CMC (MMSR-4) approves PCS or deployment once a Marine is in DES.

claim: Re-evaluation gates: light duty per chit, LIMDU at 6 months, PLD and EPLD annually
quote: Re-evaluation must be scheduled 60 days before the termination of TLD
fix: Schedule TLD re-evaluation 60 days before TLD ends. For PLD over 12 months, reevaluate and send a complete MEB to the PEB not later than 4 months before PLD expires.

claim: Marines on LIMDU are not normally deployable per 8107
quote: deployability determinations are made at the discretion of the Marine's commanding officer
fix: For TLD Marines the commanding officer decides deployability after weighing the medical officer recommendation. Once in DES/IDES, only CMC (MMSR-4) approves a deployment or PCS.

claim: PCS restriction holds the Marine at the current station during LIMDU unless the Monitor coordinates a supporting billet
quote: Marines on TLD should not execute PCS orders unless it can be assured that: a. The Marine can receive the same level of medical treatment
fix: Cite the three 8107.2 conditions. After DES entry only CMC (MMSR-4) approves PCS. Drop the Monitor role.

claim: Standard light duty runs 30 days or less and extensions beyond 30 days route to LIMDU
quote: Marines may be placed on light duty for a maximum of 90 days ... up to two periods of 30 days
fix: Light duty is up to 90 days: two 30-day periods when full duty is expected within 60 days. A Marine not returned after 60 days needs a MEB and report within the next 30 days. Never exceed 90 days.

claim: Convalescent leave coordination per 8102 (LIMDU Purpose cross-reference)
quote: The purpose of this section is to help maximize readiness by educating and integrating commanders into the DES
fix: 8102 does not address convalescent leave. Remove the cite.

claim: Medical officer chit documents light duty
quote: is documented on the SF 600 in the Marine's medical record and on a NAVMED 6310/1
fix: Name the SF 600 and NAVMED 6310/1 as the documents.

claim: PEB recommends PLD for a Marine found fit for retention with permanent restriction
quote: The CMC (MMSR-4) may retain Marines found unfit for continued naval service by the PEB on active duty in a PLD status
fix: PLD retains a Marine the PEB found unfit. The Marine submits a written request on the PEB Election of Options form or by AA form. A Marine found fit is not a PLD case.

claim: PLD carries permanent duty restrictions through the Marine's career, reflecting a permanent condition
quote: PLD is designed to retain a Marine on active duty until a specified date.
fix: PLD retains the Marine until a specified date. It also covers Marines with 16 to under 20 years who need to reach 20 years.

claim: Unit and IPAC track an annual PLD review gate per 8110
quote: Marines assigned to PLD for a period greater than 12 months ... must be reevaluated
fix: Re-evaluation applies to PLD longer than 12 months, with a complete MEB to the PEB not later than 4 months before expiry. 8110 has no annual cycle.

claim: Retirement counseling coordinated per MCO 1900.16 Chapters 2 and 7 for PLD Marines past retirement eligibility
quote: do not submit a request for retirement or transfer to the FMCR unless the PEB determines upon reevaluation that the Marine has been found fit
fix: A PLD Marine who becomes retirement eligible does not submit a retirement request unless the PEB finds the Marine fit on reevaluation.

claim: EPLD extends PLD scope for Marines with broader medical restrictions still found fit for retention through the PEB
quote: The injury/disability must be combat-related, have occurred after 11 September 2001, and meet Purple Heart criteria.
fix: EPLD is for combat wounded Marines found unfit. The injury is combat-related, after 11 Sep 2001, and meets Purple Heart criteria. CMC approves each request case by case. Enlisted submit for reenlistment under MCO 1040.31. Officers send an AA Form to MMOA-3.

claim: MCC coding reflects EPLD status
quote: assigned a draw case code (DCC) of "CW" and duty limitation codes "3" or "4"
fix: Replace MCC coding with draw case code CW and duty limitation code 3 or 4, assigned by MMEA-1 (enlisted) or MMOA-3 (officer).

claim: Monitor coordinates billet matching for EPLD
quote: Marines being retained must be capable of performing a mission in an MOS, although they may be trained in a new MOS via a lateral
fix: 8109 and MARADMIN 457/16 route EPLD requests through TFRS and an EPLD Selection Board. They name no Monitor billet match.

claim: The unit tracks the Marine, IPAC cuts transactions, MTF re-evaluates, Marine complies
quote: Appoint a Limited Duty Coordinator (SNCO or above) in writing

claim: Only Marines in bona fide light duty, TLD or PLD status are exempt from all or part of the PFT/CFT
quote: only Marines in a bona fide light duty, TLD, or PLD status are exempt from taking all or part of the PFT/CFT

claim: MTF physician has options at screening: full duty, light duty, or MEB
quote: the physician has three options

claim: Submit the active duty retirement request 6 to 18 months before the requested retirement date
quote: Submit requests for retirement/transfer to the FMCR not more than 14 months and not less than four months before the requested date.
fix: State the window as not more than 14 months and not less than 4 months before the requested date (7005.1 enlisted, 2004.1 officers). Requests outside it are rejected by MCTFS and go to CMC (MMSR-2) by separate correspondence.

claim: Submit the retirement request 6 to 18 months out
quote: Submit requests for retirement/transfer to the FMCR not more than 14 months and not less than four months before the requested date.
fix: State the window as not more than 14 months and not less than 4 months before the requested date (7005.1 enlisted, 2004.1 officers). Requests outside it are rejected by MCTFS and go to CMC (MMSR-2) by separate correspondence.

claim: Retirement requests should be submitted 6 to 18 months before the requested separation date
quote: Submit requests for retirement/transfer to the FMCR not more than 14 months and not less than four months before the requested date.
fix: State the window as not more than 14 months and not less than 4 months before the requested date (7005.1 enlisted, 2004.1 officers). Requests outside it are rejected by MCTFS and go to CMC (MMSR-2) by separate correspondence.

claim: Retirement request submission is typically 12 to 24 months before the desired retirement date
quote: Submit requests for retirement/transfer to the FMCR not more than 14 months and not less than four months before the requested date.
fix: State the window as not more than 14 months and not less than 4 months before the requested date (7005.1 enlisted, 2004.1 officers). Requests outside it are rejected by MCTFS and go to CMC (MMSR-2) by separate correspondence.

claim: Retirement request goes through the chain via Naval Letter or local form
quote: Reporting units must submit requests for retirement/transfer to the FMCR via the unit diary system
fix: Requests go in through the unit diary system in MCTFS with a signed Appendix J. Only waiver or out-of-window requests go by separate correspondence to CMC (MMSR-2).

claim: Voluntary retirement requires 20 or more years
quote: who completes 20 or more years of active duty service in the Armed Forces may request transfer to the FMCR

claim: Pre-retirement leave window typically 60 to 90 days
quote: up to 90 days of terminal leave at a CONUS command and up to 60 days if at an OCONUS command

claim: Separated with severance for rating below 30 percent
quote: Less than 30 percent disability rating with less than 20 years active service rates a medical discharge with disability severance pay.
fix: Add the less than 20 years of active service condition. A Marine with 20 or more years is not limited to severance.

claim: TRP and TAP are required under DODI 1322.29
quote: Pre-separation Counseling Brief. Must be completed not later than 365 days prior to EAS date.
fix: Cite MCO 1700.31A (2 Mar 2026) and the VOW Act. DODI 1322.29 covers SkillBridge style job training.

claim: IDES order: MEB, then IPEB, then FPEB if requested
quote: If a Marine is found unfit ... Formal PEB hearing on request

claim: Election period: member has 7 days (notification) or 30 days (board) to respond
quote: The respondent shall be provided a reasonable period of time, but not less than two working days, to respond to the notice.
fix: State the floor as not less than two working days, extendable for good cause. Drop the fixed 7 and 30 day periods.

claim: Board is three members, typically O-3 and above
quote: At least one member of the board will be in the pay grade of O-4 or above, and a majority shall be commissioned or warrant
fix: Board has at least three members. Enlisted members are E-7 or above and senior to the respondent. At least one is O-4 or above. A majority are commissioned or warrant officers.

claim: Members with 6+ years total service face board entitlement

fix: The entitlement also applies when the least favorable characterization is Other Than Honorable.

claim: Entry-level performance and conduct applies within 180 days
quote: entry-level status during the first 365 days of continuous active military service
fix: MCO 1900.16 6002 and 6205 still use 180 days. DoDI 1332.14 (1 Aug 2024) uses 365 days. Confirm with MMSR-2 before relying on 180 days.

claim: Board convening within 60 days of demand and SA decision usually 30 to 90 days
quote: If a board is required, action should be completed within 50 working days after the Marine received notification of separation.
fix: Cite the 6102 time goals: 15 working days without a board and 50 working days with a board (55 to SECNAV).

claim: MARADMIN 267/26 adds the 6303.3.a right-to-statement language and the 5.11 GO/FO review paragraph to Figures 6-2 and 6-3
quote: commands are directed to include the following statement during notification: "A statement of the Marine's right to submit statements

quote: Commanders are not authorized to dispose of any offense over which the OSTC has exercised authority unless a special trial counsel (STC) defers the offense
fix: MARADMIN 633/24 bars commanders from disposing of offenses the OSTC controls. It says nothing about separation, retirement, transfer or reenlistment processing. Cite the actual source or soften the claim.

claim: Reduction multi-grade or E-5+ requires higher authority
quote: Commanders ... may reduce enlisted Marines in the grades of PFC through Sgt per Article 15
fix: A commander reduces PFC through Sgt by NJP. Reduction authority equals promotion authority. Correct the E-5 row.

fix: Superseded flag is a false positive. MARADMIN 477/25 only schedules the FY26 SNCO board and cites MARADMIN 185/25 for cancelled obsolete messages.

claim: Administrative separation final authority is the Separation Authority, usually a GO

fix: Add the DC M&RA exception for Marines with 18 or more years (6307.1.c).

claim: Pre-Separation Counseling per the VOW Act starts at 365 days from EAS
quote: The Pre-separation Counseling Brief must be attended no later than 365 days prior to the EAS date.
fix: Say no later than 365 days. IC starts as early as 18 months out (24 for retirement). Workshops 180 days, Capstone 120 days, Commander Verification 90 days.

claim: TRP is mandatory per VOW Act and DoDI 1322.29
quote: Eligible Marines must complete the TRS requirements as outlined in this Order
fix: Cite MCO 1700.31A (2 Mar 2026). DoDI 1322.29 covers job training and SkillBridge.

claim: Retirement physical at 6 to 12 months
quote: A Marine should schedule a SHPE medical evaluation not less than six months before the effective date of separation

claim: VA disability claim at 6 months (BDD program)
fix: No archive file resolves for VA BDD timing.

claim: TRP enrollment deferred until 90 days from EAS is a failure
quote: Commander's Verification. Must be completed not later than 90 days prior to EAS date.

claim: VOW Act sets the 365 day pre-separation counseling start
fix: Statute is not in the archive. MCO 1700.31A carries the 365 day deadline.

claim: Marine 90 days from EAS triggers pre-separation counseling per MCO 1700.31
paragraph: Ch 9 para 4; Ch 8 para 4; Annex A-5
quote: The Pre-separation Counseling Brief must be attended no later than 365 days prior to the EAS date.
fix: Set the trigger at 365 days before EAS (IC and Pre-separation Counseling Brief). 90 days is the Commander Verification deadline.

claim: Marine reaches 90 days from EAS triggering pre-separation processing per 1006
quote: In no case will Marines be separated more than 90 days before their EAS without approval by the CMC (MMSR-2).
fix: 1006 limits early separation to 90 days before EAS. It sets no pre-separation trigger. Use the 365 day MCO 1700.31A deadline.

claim: Marine 12 months from EAS or retirement starts the pipeline
quote: IC must be completed no later than 365 days prior to the EAS date.

claim: The unit commander signs the separation authority action; the TAP coordinator runs DD Form 2648 per MCO 1700.31
quote: The separation authority ... is the Marine officer having general court-martial convening authority (GCMCA) over the respondent
fix: The separation authority is the GCMCA or the authority named in Tables 6-2 and 6-3. The unit commander recommends. MCO 1700.31A (2 Mar 2026) replaces 1700.31 and assigns TRP personnel and the UTC.

claim: DD Form 214 prepared in MOL DTMS
quote: Documents prepared using DTMS in MOL will automatically carry over

claim: S-1 officer signs Block 21 as officer authorized to sign; Marine signs Block 20
quote: 21a. MEMBER SIGNATURE. The Marine being separated will sign all copies in black ink
fix: Block 21a is the Marine signature. Block 22a is the Official Authorized to Sign, appointed in writing at E-7/GS-7 or above (no lower than E-5/GS-5 with a documented reason). Block 20 is the copy 6 request to the state VA office.

claim: Reservists releasing from active duty for more than 30 consecutive days also trigger a DD Form 214
quote: Separation from a period of active duty, active duty for training (ADT), full-time training duty, or Active Duty Operational Support (ADOS) of 90 days or
fix: A Reservist gets a DD Form 214 at 90 days or more of active duty, IADT, AR separation, or a contingency order of any length. Under 90 days gets none unless 1202.3.b applies.

claim: Block 24 is character of service
quote: 24. CHARACTER OF SERVICE. Enter in CAPITAL LETTERS the appropriate character of service.

claim: Block 26 separation code and Block 28 narrative reason; Block 27 reentry code
quote: 28. NARRATIVE REASON FOR SEPARATION. This is a brief statement describing the circumstances of the termination.

claim: Block 13 holds decorations, medals and badges
quote: 13. DECORATIONS, MEDALS, BADGES, COMMENDATIONS, CITATIONS AND CAMPAIGN RIBBONS AWARDED OR AUTHORIZED.

claim: Block 18 remarks capture combat service and HDP designations
quote: Participation in contingency operations ... will also be credited with contingency operation participation on their DD Form 214.
fix: Block 18 lists contingency operation participation. HDP is not named in the block 18 instructions.

claim: Administrative separation board is mandatory at six or more years of service or when OTH is the least favorable characterization
quote: A statement of the right to request an administrative board if the Marine has six or more years of total active and inactive-service
fix: The Marine has the right to request a board and has the option to waive it. Failure to respond is a waiver. Say entitlement, not mandatory.

claim: Board entitlement attaches at six or more years or when OTH is the least favorable characterization
quote: right to request an administrative board if the Marine has six or more years of total active and inactive-service

quote: 6102. PROCESSING TIME GOALS

claim: MARADMIN 189/26 para 9.b holds processing in abeyance for another admin separation and requires MPO notice within 24 hours
quote: Commanders shall notify MPO within 24 hours if a Marine, undergoing administrative processing under this MARADMIN, concurrently becomes subject to administrative separation

claim: The unit commander initiates officer administrative separation and notifies the officer per 4101
quote: The CMC shall initiate processing for administrative separation under the following circumstances
fix: The commanding officer reports incidents to CMC (JPL) under 4101. CMC initiates processing under 4102. Rewrite the commander role as reporting.

claim: Officer may submit resignation in lieu of show cause (4104); SecNav decides
quote: An officer being processed for separation for cause may, at any time during proceedings under this Chapter, submit a qualified or unqualified resignation

claim: MARADMIN 189/26: CDA is sole show-cause authority and JDK2 applies to officers

fix: Use DD Form 2656 for the SBP election. It goes to DFAS at least 30 days before retirement (1406.1).

claim: 30+ years retire to the Retired List; 20 to 30 years transfer to the FMCR
quote: An enlisted Marine ... who applies for retirement after completing 30 or more years of active service in the Armed Forces shall be retired.

claim: SBP election is required and irrevocable at retirement
quote: If no election is made prior to the effective date of the retirement, DFAS (by law) will automatically deduct full SBP coverage
fix: 1406 does not say irrevocable. Counseling is required. Election other than full coverage needs notarized spousal concurrence.

claim: 60-day career cap on leave sell
fix: 7011 and 1010 do not state a sell-back cap. 1010.2.b allows 90 days terminal leave CONUS and 60 OCONUS.

claim: Modification of FMCR/retirement date routes through MMSR

quote: Officers with more than 20 years of active duty may request retirement.
fix: Add the service-in-grade table: CWO2-5 2 years, 2ndLt/1stLt 6 months, Capt/Maj 2 years, LtCol-Gen 3 years.

claim: Spouse concurs in any SBP election less than full coverage; missed election gives default full coverage
quote: Elections other than full coverage require spousal concurrence and must be notarized.

quote: Requests ... will be submitted by the reporting command via the Unit Diary Marine Integrated Personnel System
